mainTopic: A minor's betrothal without her father's consent, and betrothing a woman with several dates
overview: The amud opens by closing an earlier argument: the גמרא sides with the junior scholar, and רבא explains why רב הונא held his view. Next comes a new dispute about a קטנה who accepted קידושין without her father's consent. רב says both she and her father can block it, while רב אסי says only her father can. A ברייתא about a מפותה is brought against רב אסי, but רב himself shows it is no proof, and רב יוסף and אביי argue over how to read it. Then a new משנה teaches how a man betroths a woman with several dates, and how the exact wording decides whether their values add up to a פרוטה. The גמרא ties the first case to רבי שמעון's rule about oaths. It then struggles over which case the 'eating one by one' clause belongs to, and רבי יוחנן admits he cannot explain it. רב and שמואל answer that it belongs to the first case, while רבי אמי says it belongs to the joined case and only the last date counts. רבא learns rules about betrothing with a loan from רבי אמי, and the third rule continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The student's view is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes an earlier argument by saying the view of the 'student' seems correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words of the student seem correct.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an argument from the previous section. It says the opinion of the junior scholar makes the most sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'student' is the junior scholar, רב ירמיה בר אבא, who argued with the more senior רב הונא. Even though he was junior, the גמרא finds his position more convincing. That closes the earlier back-and-forth.

keyTerms.meaning: student; here, the junior scholar in the argument

phrases.english: The words of the student seem correct.
phrases.notes: The 'student' is the junior scholar from the argument just before this, set against the more senior רב הונא.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי תַלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the dispute from the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The junior scholar's opinion is accepted over רב הונא's.

steps.title: רבא explains רב הונא's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains רב הונא's view: the girl is treated like a יתומה even though her father is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רב הונא's reason? Since an act was done with her as if she were an orphan, even while her father was alive.
steps.whatsHappening: Even though רב הונא's view was not accepted, רבא explains the thinking behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The girl went ahead with her marriage on her own, as if she had no father to decide for her, and her father did nothing to stop it. רב הונא therefore treats her like a יתומה, an orphan, whose marriage is valid with her own consent. This shows his view was a reasonable one, even if it was not followed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא –
phrases.english: Rava said: What is the reason of Rav Huna?
Since an act of an orphan was done with her
phrases.notes: In other words, she acted as if no father was there to decide for her.

phrases.english: during the father's lifetime.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב הונא's view, the גמרא explains why he held it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא views the girl like a יתומה because she acted on her own while her father ignored it.

steps.title: Dispute: who can cancel a minor's betrothal done without her father
steps.stepSummary: רב says both the girl and her father can block the betrothal; רב אסי says only her father can.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: A minor girl who was betrothed without her father's knowledge. רב said: both she and her father can block it. רב אסי said: her father can, but not she.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a dispute between אמוראים about a קטנה who accepted קידושין without her father's consent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees her father can stop the קידושין from taking effect. The argument is about the girl herself. רב lets her back out too. רב אסי says she cannot, since she agreed to it in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: it was stated; it opens a dispute between אמוראים
a girl who is a minor
without her father's knowledge or consent
to block, to prevent it from taking effect

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute is the subject of everything that follows in this section, including the challenge from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: It was stated: A minor girl who was betrothed
without her father's knowledge,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: בֵּין הִיא וּבֵין אָבִיהָ
phrases.english: Rav said: Both she and her father
are able to block it.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: אָבִיהָ וְלֹא הִיא.
phrases.english: And Rav Asi said: Her father, but not she.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: קְטַנָּה שֶׁנִּתְקַדְּשָׁה שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, separate from the earlier dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: both the girl and her father can cancel. רב אסי: only the father can.

steps.title: A challenge to רב אסי from the seduced girl
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a seduced girl herself can refuse to marry the seducer, which seems to contradict רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא challenged רב אסי (some say it was חייא בר רב): The פסוק says 'If her father utterly refuses.' This teaches only about her father. How do we know she herself can refuse? The פסוק repeats 'refuse, refuse' to teach that the refusal can come from anyone.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone attacks רב אסי using a ברייתא about a מפותה, a girl who was seduced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled word 'מאן ימאן' teaches that the girl herself, not only her father, can refuse to marry the seducer. She went along with him at first, yet she can still back out. That seems to show a girl can undo something she agreed to, which goes against רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenged him (from a תנאי source)
in any case; no matter who refuses

phrases.english: Rav Huna challenged Rav Asi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: and some say it was Ḥiyya bar Rav who challenged Rav Asi:
"If her father utterly refuses":
I have only her father;
from where do I know that she herself can refuse?
The verse teaches: "If he refuses, refuses" —
in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אסי's side of the dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling that the girl herself cannot cancel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A seduced girl agreed at first and can still refuse, so a girl can undo what she agreed to.

steps.title: רב rejects the proof that seems to help him
steps.stepSummary: רב says the ברייתא is no proof, since it could be speaking about a seduction not meant as marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to them: Don't follow a proof that can be turned around. He can answer you: this is a case where the man seduced her not for the sake of marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: רב himself steps in and says the challenge against רב אסי does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seducer never meant the act as קידושין, there is no betrothal at all. So when she refuses to marry him, she is not undoing anything, and the ברייתא says nothing about our case.

keyTerms.meaning: don't go after the reverse; don't use a proof that can be flipped
to answer, to give an alternative reading

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get confused: רב is the one who holds the girl can cancel, and yet he is the one knocking down the proof for his own view. He is being honest that the ברייתא does not prove it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב: לָא תֵּיזְלוּ בָּתַר אִיפְּכָא.
phrases.english: Rav said to them: Do not go after the reverse.
phrases.notes: He means: don't rely on a source that can just as easily be read the other way.

phrases.english: He can answer you:
For example, where he seduced her not for the sake of marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב: לָא תֵּיזְלוּ בָּתַר אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב אסי against the challenge in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא of the מפותה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be speaking about a case with no קידושין at all.

steps.title: Why would a verse be needed for that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסוק would be needed to teach that she can refuse when no marriage was ever intended.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he seduced her not for the sake of marriage, do we need a verse for that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there was never any קידושין, of course she does not have to marry him. A special teaching from the doubled word would then seem pointless.

phrases.english: He seduced her not for the sake of marriage —
is a verse needed?

steps.triggerLanguage: פִּיתָּהּ שֶׁלֹּא לְשׁוּם אִישׁוּת קְרָא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as a seduction not for marriage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is obvious, so the פסוק would be teaching nothing.

steps.title: The verse teaches that he still pays the fine
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the פסוק teaches the seducer pays the קנס even when she is the one who refuses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It teaches that he pays the fine of a seducer.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given to the question in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is not that she may refuse; it is about the money. Even when she refuses, and not her father, the seducer still owes the קנס of a מפותה.

keyTerms.meaning: a fixed fine set by the תורה

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
To say that he pays the fine like a seducer of a girl.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לוֹמַר שֶׁמְּשַׁלֵּם קְנָס כִּמְפוּתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a new purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק would only be teaching that she may refuse, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that the fine is owed even when she is the one who refuses.

steps.title: רב יוסף supports this from another ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the reading fits a ברייתא that requires the seducer to give קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: If so, that is what we learned: 'He shall pay a dowry for her to be his wife' teaches that she needs קידושין from him. If he had seduced her for the sake of marriage, why would she need קידושין?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings support for reading the case as a seduction not meant for marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another ברייתא says the seducer must give her קידושין. If the act itself had been meant as marriage, it would already count as קידושין. So the ברייתא must be talking about a seduction that was not meant as marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: he shall surely pay a dowry for her

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: אִי הָכִי,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him: If so,
this is what we learned:
"He shall surely pay a dowry for her to be his wife" —
that she requires betrothal from him.
And if he seduced her for the sake of marriage,
why do I need betrothal?
phrases.notes: The act itself would already have made her betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דִּתְנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading from steps 5 and 7.
steps.raayaObject: Reading the מפותה case as a seduction not for marriage
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'מהר ימהרנה' that requires קידושין

steps.title: אביי: she needs betrothal with her father's consent
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof: even if it was meant as marriage, she needs new קידושין with her father's consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: She needs קידושין with her father's consent.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act may have been meant as marriage, but it happened without her father's consent, because she is a קטנה. That is why new קידושין are needed. So the ברייתא does not prove the seduction was not for marriage.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of the מפותה is no clear proof in the dispute between רב and רב אסי, and רב יוסף's support for reading it as 'not for marriage' is answered by אביי.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
She requires betrothal with her father's consent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: צְרִיכָה קִידּוּשִׁין לְדַעַת אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's support in step 8.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The need for קידושין can be explained by the lack of her father's consent, even if the act was meant as marriage.

steps.title: The משנה: Betrothing a woman with several dates
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives three cases of קידושין with dates and says when a single date must be worth a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man says to a woman, 'Be betrothed to me with this date,' and then, 'Be betrothed to me with this one,' she is betrothed if one of the dates is worth a פרוטה, and if not, she is not betrothed. If he says, 'With this, and this, and this,' she is betrothed if all of them together are worth a פרוטה, and if not, she is not. If she was eating them one by one, she is not betrothed unless one of them is worth a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes three ways a man might try to marry a woman by giving her several dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he says 'be betrothed to me' for each date, each date is its own separate attempt, so one date alone must be worth a פרוטה. When he links them with 'and this, and this,' they count as one combined gift, so their total can reach a פרוטה. The third case, where she eats them one by one, again needs one date worth a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth a פרוטה, the smallest value that can make קידושין work

steps.confusionAlert: Repeating the words 'be betrothed to me' for each date splits the dates into separate attempts. Saying 'and this, and this' joins them into one. The wording decides whether the values can be added together.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who says to a woman, 'Be betrothed to me with this date,'
'Be betrothed to me with this one'

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: if one of them is worth a פרוטה, she is betrothed,
and if not, she is not betrothed.
'With this, and with this, and with this'

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה בְּכוּלָּן – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: if all of them together are worth a פרוטה, she is betrothed,
and if not, she is not betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה אוֹכֶלֶת רִאשׁוֹנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה – אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: If she was eating them one by one, she is not betrothed,
phrases.notes: Literally 'first, first.' She ate each date as soon as she got it.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה.
phrases.english: unless one of them is worth a פרוטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹמֵר לְאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the earlier discussion about the seducer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separate statements of 'be betrothed to me' need one date worth a פרוטה. A joined statement lets the dates add up. If she ate them one by one, one date must be worth a פרוטה.

steps.title: Which תנא holds that repeating the phrase splits the betrothal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the first case of the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught that saying 'be betrothed to me, be betrothed to me' for each date makes each one separate?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking which תנא stands behind the first case of the משנה. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats each repeated 'be betrothed to me' as its own separate act. The גמרא wants to know who holds that repeating the key words splits one act into several.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught this? (which תנא's opinion is it)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Who taught
'Be betrothed,' 'be betrothed'?
phrases.notes: He means the first case, where he said 'be betrothed to me' for each date.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion the first clause of the משנה follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that repeating the betrothal phrase makes each item a separate act.

steps.title: רבה: It is רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the first case follows רבי שמעון, who says that only a repeated oath-word makes each oath separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is רבי שמעון, who said that a person is not liable separately unless he says the word 'oath' for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that the first case of the משנה follows רבי שמעון. He bases this on רבי שמעון's rule about oaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that repeating the key word, 'oath,' is what turns one statement into several separate ones. In the same way, repeating 'be betrothed to me' turns each date into its own act of קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view is applied here

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is Rabbi Shimon,
who said: unless he says 'oath'
phrases.notes: This is about someone who swore falsely about several things. רבי שמעון counts them separately only if he said 'oath' for each one.

phrases.english: for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first clause follows רבי שמעון: repeating the key word makes separate acts.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same principle about repeated wording applies both to oaths and to קידושין.

steps.title: Which case does the eating clause refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second case and asks which earlier case the 'eating one by one' clause belongs to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'With this, and this, and this,' if all of them together are worth a פרוטה, and so on. To which case does the eating clause refer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second case of the משנה. It then asks which case the last clause, about eating the dates one by one, is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never says whether the eating case continues the first case (separate statements) or the second (joined statement). The גמרא is setting up a test of both options.

keyTerms.meaning: To which one? (which clause is meant)

phrases.english: 'With this, and with this, and with this'

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בְּכוּלָּן שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: if all of them together are worth a פרוטה, etc.
To which does it refer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהֵיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to clarify its last clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the eating clause belongs to the first case or the second case.

steps.title: It cannot refer to the first case
steps.stepSummary: If the eating case belonged to the first case, there would be no reason to mention eating at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to the first case, why mention specifically that she ate them? Even if she put them down, the law would be the same, because he said 'be betrothed to me with this' for each one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and rejects it. In the first case each date already needs to be worth a פרוטה, so eating adds nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case every date is its own act of קידושין, so one date must be worth a פרוטה whether she eats it or not. Mentioning eating would teach nothing, so the clause cannot belong to the first case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces an option the גמרא is about to test)

phrases.english: If you say it refers to the first clause,
why specifically 'she ate'?
Even if she put them down, the same applies,
since he is saying 'be betrothed to me with this'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אַרֵישָׁא, מַאי אִירְיָא אוֹכֶלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and knocks out the first option raised in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the eating clause belongs to the first case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the first case each date already needs a פרוטה, so mentioning eating would be pointless.

steps.title: It refers to the latter case
steps.stepSummary: The eating clause must belong to the second case, where the dates were joined together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to the latter clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the eating case continues the second case. Normally those dates can add up, but if she ate them one by one, one date must be worth a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating makes a difference only where the dates would otherwise combine. If she eats them as she gets them, they are never all together, so they no longer add up.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the latter clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question of step 13 after the first option failed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the clause in the other case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The eating clause might belong to the first case.
steps.terutzMaskana: It belongs to the joined case: eating one by one stops the dates from adding up.

steps.title: But the first date is only a loan!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how even the first date could work, since until he finishes giving all of them, each date counts only as a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is she betrothed even with the first one? But it is a loan!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just explained. In the joined case, how can the first date she ate ever make her betrothed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the joined case, the קידושין is meant to happen only once all the dates are given. Until then each date is like a loan, and a woman cannot be betrothed with a loan. By the end the first date has already been eaten, so it seems it can never work.

phrases.english: And even with the first one?
But it is a loan!
phrases.notes: Until he finishes giving all the dates, he could take each one back, so each one is treated like a loan.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּקַמַּיְיתָא? וְהָא מִלְוָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of the eating clause as explained in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that she is betrothed if one date, even the first one, is worth a פרוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before all the dates are given, each one is a loan, and a loan cannot make קידושין; the first date is gone by the end.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Everything is here, yet we cannot explain it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן admits that he cannot answer the question: everything in the משנה is clear, but he cannot explain it. Steps 18 and 19 then give two answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Here is a table, here is meat, and here is a knife, but we have no mouth to eat!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן responds to the question with a picture. Everything we need is in front of us, yet we cannot make sense of this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the משנה are clear, but neither reading works. On the first case, mentioning eating seems pointless (step 14). On the second case, the eaten dates are only a loan (step 16). רבי יוחנן does not solve this himself; the next two steps bring answers from רב and שמואל and from רבי אמי.

keyTerms.meaning: And we have no mouth to eat; we cannot make use of what is in front of us

steps.whatToRemember: Each placement of the eating clause runs into a problem: on the first case eating seems pointless, and on the joined case the eaten dates are only a loan. רבי יוחנן admits he cannot explain it. Two answers follow: רב and שמואל put the clause back on the first case (step 18), and רבי אמי reads 'one of them' as 'the last one' (step 19).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's words are not an answer to the question. They are an honest admission that he cannot answer it. The answers come from רב and שמואל and from רבי אמי in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Here is a table, and here is meat,
and here is a knife,
and we have no mouth to eat!
phrases.notes: The word 'mouth' in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי שֻׁלְחָן, וַהֲרֵי בָּשָׂר, וַהֲרֵי סַכִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question of step 16, together with step 14, by admitting he cannot explain the משנה; steps 18 and 19 answer it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן cannot explain the eating clause under either reading; answers follow from רב and שמואל and from רבי אמי.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: the eating clause belongs to the first case after all
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל say the eating clause refers to the first case, where each date was given separately. The משנה is teaching a bigger חידוש: even when she eats right away, a date worth less than a פרוטה does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both said: Really, it goes on the first case, and the משנה uses a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that when she sets the dates aside, she is betrothed only if one is worth a פרוטה. But when she eats them, since she enjoys them right away, you might think she decides to give herself over even for less. So the משנה teaches us that she still is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new answer from רב and שמואל. It goes back to the option the גמרא rejected earlier: the eating clause belongs to the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 14) the גמרא asked why eating would matter in the first case. רב and שמואל answer that eating is mentioned to cancel a mistaken idea. Because she benefits right away, we might have thought she agrees to be betrothed even for less than a פרוטה. The משנה tells us no: she still needs a date worth a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually, going back to an option that was set aside
The first clause of the משנה
'There is no need to say': the obvious case is mentioned on the way to a bigger חידוש
She makes up her mind and gives herself over

steps.confusionAlert: In a 'לא מיבעיא' structure, the easy case comes first and the real חידוש comes second. Here the חידוש is the eating case: even then she is not betrothed with less than a פרוטה.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel both said:
Really, it refers to the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the case where he betrothed her with each date separately.

phrases.english: and it is speaking in a 'no need to say' style:
there is no need to say this where she sets them down,
that if one is worth a peruta, yes, she is betrothed,
and if not, no.
But where she is eating them,
since her benefit comes right away,
I might say she decides and gives herself over,
so it teaches us that she does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: לְעוֹלָם אַרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer where רבי יוחנן had none. It revives the first-case reading that step 14 had rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the clause as a 'לא מיבעיא' teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because she benefits right away by eating, she might be betrothed even for less than a פרוטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even when she eats, she is betrothed only if a single date is worth a פרוטה.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the eating clause belongs to the second case, and only the last date counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי keeps the eating clause on the second case. He reads 'one of them' as 'the last one', because the earlier dates she already ate were only a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Really, it goes on the second case. What does 'unless one of them is worth a פרוטה' mean? It means unless the last one is worth a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives a different answer. He solves the problem from step 16 by saying the משנה means the last date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 asked how any date could work, since each one is only a loan until he finishes giving them all. רבי אמי agrees that the eaten dates are a loan. The last date, however, is a real gift at the moment the giving is finished. So if the last date is worth a פרוטה, she is betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of the משנה
The last one, here the last date
Worth a פרוטה, the minimum value for קידושין

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Really, it refers to the latter clause,
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the case where he betrothed her with all the dates together.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי ״עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה״ –
phrases.english: and what does 'unless one of them is worth a peruta' mean?
Unless the last one is worth a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer, different from רב and שמואל's. It keeps the reading of step 15 and answers step 16 by reinterpreting the words 'one of them'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording ('one of them' means 'the last one')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any one of the dates worth a פרוטה could make the קידושין work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the last date counts, because the earlier eaten dates were only a loan.

steps.title: רבא draws lessons from רבי אמי's explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבא says three rulings can be learned from רבי אמי. Two appear here: קידושין with a loan does not work, and when a man gives a loan plus a פרוטה, her mind is on the פרוטה. The third comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Learn three things from רבי אמי. Learn from it that if someone betroths with a loan, she is not betrothed. And learn from it that if someone betroths with a loan and a פרוטה, her mind is on the פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes רבי אמי's answer and pulls out general rules from it. This step lists the first two, and the גמרא continues with the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule 1: The eaten dates do not count, because they were a loan. This shows that קידושין with a loan does not work. Rule 2: The eaten dates (a loan) together with the last date (a פרוטה) still work. This shows that her mind is on the פרוטה, so the קידושין takes effect through it.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: a conclusion drawn from a statement
One who betroths with a loan (letting her keep money she owes him)
Her mind is on the פרוטה

steps.whyThisMatters: These are general rules of קידושין that reach far beyond the case of dates: a loan alone does not work, but a loan plus a פרוטה does.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Learn three things from Rabbi Ami's statement.
Learn from it: one who betroths with a loan,
she is not betrothed,
And learn from it: one who betroths with a loan and a peruta,
her mind is on the peruta,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי תְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds directly on רבי אמי's answer and draws general rulings from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין with a loan alone does not work. With a loan plus a פרוטה, she is betrothed, because her mind is on the פרוטה.
